visual_text: 37.5°C scores 0 on NEWS2. For this person it is a 1.5°C rise.
Fever rule: more than 1.1°C above usual
US care home guidance counts a rise of more than 1.1°C above usual as a fever.
Compare the reading with the person's usual temperature.
A low score should never override a professional's or carer's concern.
High et al., Clin Infect Dis 2009; Stone et al., 2012; RCP NEWS2 2017 via Engebretsen et al., 2020; Williams, Clin Med 2022
alt_text: Two vertical temperature scales from 34 to 40 degrees C. Left: NEWS2 points, with 36.1 to 38.0 scoring 0 (hatched). Right, an illustrative person with usual 36.0 and reading 37.5, a 1.5 degree rise bracketed in orange and a dashed line at 37.1 for the care home fever rule. A reading of 37.5 scores 0 yet is a rise for this person.
